replays.label: Webinar Replay
replays.title: From RSUs to Real Assets
replays.subtitle: How SaaS Engineering Leaders Reduce Risk with Real Estate
takeaways: Holding vested RSUs in employer stock ties your income, career, and net worth to the same company.
Diversifying is a planned allocation decision, not a reaction to a price drop or a tax bill.
Passive multifamily lets you own real assets without becoming a landlord, because an experienced operator runs the property.
Before moving equity into real estate, decide how much capital, for how long, and what role it plays in your portfolio.

replays.label: Webinar Replay
replays.title: The Second Engine
replays.subtitle: Building Wealth Beyond Salary, Bonus, and Equity
takeaways: Multifamily can create cash flow, appreciation, and tax advantages.
Multifamily offers a faster path to scale than single family investing.
The right multifamily strategy can reduce dependence on salary, bonus, and equity.
Wealth grows by consistently acquiring income producing apartment assets.

replays.label: Webinar Replay
replays.title: The Due Diligence Framework
replays.subtitle: How to Assess Risk, Operator Quality, and Deal Fit
takeaways: A projected return is only as reliable as the assumptions and risks behind it.
The operator deserves its own underwriting: track record, alignment, reporting, and how problems get handled.
Deal fit matters as much as deal quality. Liquidity, time horizon, and portfolio role have to match your goals.
A repeatable diligence process gives you the confidence to pass on deals that look good but are wrong for you.

replays.label: Webinar Replay
replays.title: Rise Sunridge
replays.subtitle: Income, Tax Efficiency, and Downside Protection in One Deal
takeaways: A strong deal should be evaluated as a full strategy, not just by projected returns.
Rise Sunridge's income story came from the property, market demand, operating plan, and distribution structure.
Tax efficiency can improve investor outcomes when the deal structure aligns with the investor's tax situation.
Downside protection comes from how the deal is underwritten, financed, reserved, operated, and matched to the right investor profile.

replays.label: Webinar Replay
replays.title: Multifamily vs. Build to Rent vs. Self Storage
replays.subtitle: Which Offers the Best Mix of Income, Tax Efficiency, and Risk Control?
takeaways: Each asset class has strengths, but they are not equal in simplicity, stability, or investor fit.
Multifamily's income advantage comes from essential housing demand, diversified rent rolls, and operational scale.
Tax benefits can exist across real estate, but multifamily often provides a clear depreciation and cost segregation story.
For many passive investors, multifamily may offer the most balanced combination of income, tax efficiency, risk control, and understandability.

replays.label: Replay · September 2026
replays.title: Escape Capital Gains. Escape Concentration.
replays.subtitle: The Passive 1031 Strategy for Engineering Leaders
takeaways: A 1031 exchange can help investors defer taxes, but planning must begin before the sale closes.
The exchange process is deadline driven and requires coordination with a qualified intermediary, CPA, attorney, and investment team.
A 1031 exchange can be used to reposition capital from management heavy properties into more passive real estate options.
Not every syndication can accept 1031 exchange funds, so investors need to understand the structure before assuming it qualifies.

replays.label: Replay · October 22, 2026
replays.title: From RSUs to Real Assets
replays.subtitle: How One Investor Turned $200,000 Into $600 a Month in Tax Sheltered Distributions
takeaways: Projected returns are only as credible as the assumptions behind them.
One investor used this same evaluation process to convert vested RSUs into tax sheltered monthly cash flow.
A strong review process should make risks, assumptions, accountability, and execution more visible.
Moving wealth out of employer stock still requires a clear allocation and diligence process.
